findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences a possibly-empty destination list
findings.description: Line 118 takes the first destination with `?? []`, then line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, the destructured value is `undefined` and this throws. Both inputs occur: `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` sets `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a calendar, and `confirm.handler.ts:176-180` sets `[]`. `MeetLocationType` is `"integrations:google:meet"` (`packages/app-store/locations.ts:54`), so any Meet booking without a connected calendar throws. `eventManager.create` is unguarded at `handleNewBooking.ts:2114`, so the booking fails. The pre-diff code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, and the fallback exists for exactly this case. The type checker won't flag it: the repo has no `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so the destructured element is typed non-undefined. Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback is always `undefined`
findings.description:
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares `cal.externalId` against `null` or `undefined`. `DestinationCalendar.externalId` is a required `String` (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:153`), so the match never succeeds and the expression always returns `undefined`. The same expression is at lines 315-317 in `deleteEvent`. The pre-diff code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so this is a regression:
- `updateEvent` passes `calendarId: undefined` to `events.update` (lines 258-261). This is reached whenever a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, which `EventManager.ts:505-509` passes through as `null`.
- `deleteEvent` falls back to `"primary"` (line 322). The event stays in the real destination calendar after a cancel, and the resulting 404 is resolved silently (line 335).

Fix: fall back to the calendar the event was created in, such as `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, or match on the credential if the caller passes one.

findings.title: Google `createEvent` writes legacy destinations to `primary`
findings.description:
The target calendar is now chosen by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable (`schema.prisma:159`), and the code treats credential-less rows as live: `EventManager.ts:375-381` has an `else` branch "for bookings made before the refactor". For those rows the `find` never matches, so the event goes to `"primary"` instead of the selected calendar. Three follow-on effects:
1. The organizer attendee email (lines 122-124) still uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which names a calendar the event isn't in.
2. The reference is saved without `externalCalendarId` (`EventManager.ts:169` reads `result.externalId`, which is undefined on this path), so later updates hit the broken fallback above.
3. `calendar.events.patch` (lines 166-168) passes raw `selectedCalendar`. Unlike `insert` at line 154, it has no `|| "primary"`, so it is called with `calendarId: undefined` when a Hangout link is returned and no credential matches.

Fix: resolve the target calendar once (credential match, then legacy row, then primary) and use that value for insert, patch, and the organizer email.

findings.title: Office365, Lark, and iCal/CalDAV ignore per-credential targeting
findings.description: Only Google was moved to per-credential targeting. Office365 `createEvent` (line 73) and Lark `createEvent` (lines 128-129) and `createAttendees` (lines 164-165) all use `destinationCalendar[0]` for every credential. For a collective event with a second Office365 or Lark host, `createAllCalendarEvents` (`EventManager.ts:339-371`) posts to the first host's calendar. The error is caught in `CalendarManager.ts:237-254` and returned as `success: false`. `create()` persists every result, failures included (`EventManager.ts:153-172`), so the failed attempt becomes a reference with `uid: ""`, the second host's `credentialId`, and the first host's `externalCalendarId`. iCal/CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-165`) is worse: it filters calendars by the first destination's `externalId`, which matches nothing on the second account, so it reports success and creates nothing. The contract `Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId)` (`packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221`) asks each integration to re-derive the target from `event.destinationCalendar`, even though `CalendarManager.createEvent` already has the resolved `externalId` and does not pass it down. Fix: pass the resolved external ID through the interface, use it in every integration, and decide whether failed attempts should be persisted as references.

findings.title: Collective team calendars are dropped when the organizer has no calendar
findings.description: `destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (lines 1063-1067). Line 1078 then calls `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which does nothing. The team members' calendars for COLLECTIVE events are silently dropped in that case. The collection is also built as a side effect inside `users.slice(1).map(...)` (lines 990-994), which makes the flow harder to follow. Fix: start from `[]` and build the array explicitly.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel deletes now run once per calendar reference
findings.description: The `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop (line 423) now wraps the recurring branch (lines 444-468). That branch deletes every updated booking's event on every calendar credential, so with N calendar references each delete runs N times. The `.find` at line 454 also picks only the first calendar reference per updated booking. Before this diff the recurring branch ran once. Fix: move the recurring deletion out of the per-reference loop.

findings.title: `loadUsers` catch replaces the real error
findings.description:
The catch maps every error to a fixed status and never logs the original:
- An `HttpError` with its own status (404, 403) becomes a 400.
- A `PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, which is a database failure, becomes a 400 that blames the client.
- Everything else, including the validation error thrown at line 728 for an empty `dynamicUserList`, becomes `500 "Unable to load users"`. The specific message never reaches the caller, and nothing is logged.

Fix: rethrow `HttpError` unchanged, map validation errors explicitly, log unexpected errors before returning the 500, and drop the 400 mapping for Prisma errors.

findings.title: Calendar-update failures are no longer logged
findings.description: The `console.error(message)` was removed from the catch. The `message` string is still built (lines 592-595) but never used, so failures become `success: false` results with no log. Restore the log and remove the dead variable.

findings.title: Credential lookups by ID don't check ownership
findings.description: When the owner's credentials don't include a reference's `credentialId`, the code loads the credential by ID alone (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id } })`) and uses its key to call the external calendar API. `EventManager.ts:341-355` and `511-530` do the same. Before this diff, only the owner's credentials were used. Booking references are server-written, so the practical risk is low, but the lookup should be scoped, for example to the booking's team. Separately, in `updateAllCalendarEvents`, if the DB lookup finds nothing, `credential` stays `undefined` and is passed to `updateEvent`, which reads `credential.appName` (`CalendarManager.ts:318`).

findings.title: Destination normalization and credential lookup are copy-pasted
findings.description: The `x.destinationCalendar ? [x.destinationCalendar] : x.user.destinationCalendar ? [...] : []` normalization is repeated at about a dozen call sites: `handleCancelBooking.ts:251-255` and `528-532`, `confirm.handler.ts:176-180`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts:290-295`, `editLocation.handler.ts:85-90`, `paypal-webhook.ts:152-156`, `webhook.ts` (twice), `bookingReminder.ts`, and `requestReschedule.handler.ts`. The "load credential from DB and map to `CredentialWithAppName`" block is duplicated at `EventManager.ts:341-368` and `511-541`, and `handleCancelBooking.ts:428-441` adds a third variant. The normalization also disagrees on its fallback, `null` in `handleNewBooking` and `[]` elsewhere, which is what makes finding 5 possible. Fix: one `toDestinationCalendars(booking, user)` helper and one `loadCalendarCredential(id)` helper.

findings.title: No tests cover the new behavior
findings.description: The only test change in the diff is an expectation update in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249`. There is no `EventManager` test, and the only core test file (`CalendarManager.test.ts`) covers `getCalendarCredentials`. Nothing exercises multi-destination create/update, the Google credential match, the legacy destination path, the Meet fallback with empty destinations (which would have caught the first finding), the `handleCancelBooking` DB fallback, or the collective merge. These should be written as failing tests first, then made to pass.

findings.title: Scheduling type is compared two different ways
findings.description: `isTeamEventType` now compares against string literals, but `SchedulingType` is still imported (line 71) and used on line 805. The collective checks at lines 992 and 1077 also use the `"COLLECTIVE"` literal. Use the enum throughout.

findings.title: Unrelated changes are mixed into this diff
findings.description: The diff also changes the user-visible text "organiser" to "organizer" (line 230), renames `orginalBookingDuration`, changes the import style in `builder.ts`, rewrites the `create.handler.ts` spreads, and removes `organization: { select: { slug } }` from the dynamic-user select in `handleNewBooking.ts`. I found no consumer of the removed relation in `handleNewBooking.ts`, and `getBookerUrl` reads `organizationId`, so nothing obviously breaks. These changes don't belong in a destination-calendar change and would be cleaner as a separate commit.
